verses.text: These are the words of the covenant which Yahweh commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant which he made with them in Horeb.
Moses called to all Israel, and said to them: Your eyes have seen all that Yahweh did in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land;
the great trials which your eyes saw, the signs, and those great wonders.
But Yahweh has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.
I have led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes have not grown old on you, and your shoes have not grown old on your feet.
You have not eaten bread, neither have you drunk wine or strong drink; that you may know that I am Yahweh your God.
When you came to this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, came out against us to battle, and we struck them.
We took their land, and gave it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.
Therefore keep the words of this covenant and do them, that you may prosper in all that you do.
All of you stand today in the presence of Yahweh your God; your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, even all the men of Israel,
your little ones, your wives, and the foreigners who are in the middle of your camps, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water;
that you may enter into the covenant of Yahweh your God, and into his oath, which Yahweh your God makes with you today;
that he may establish you today as his people, and that he may be your God, as he spoke to you, and as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
Neither do I make this covenant and this oath with you only,
but with those who stand here with us today before Yahweh our God, and also with those who are not here with us today
(for you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we came through the middle of the nations through which you passed;
and you have seen their abominations, and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which were among them);

lest there should be among you man, woman, family, or tribe whose heart turns away today from Yahweh our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations; lest there should be among you a root that produces bitter poison;

and it happen, when he hears the words of this curse, that he bless himself in his heart, saying, “I shall have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart, to destroy the moist with the dry.”

Yahweh will not pardon him, but then Yahweh’s anger and his jealousy will smoke against that man, and all the curse that is written in this book will fall on him, and Yahweh will blot out his name from under the sky.
Yahweh will set him apart for evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant that is written in this book of the law.

The generation to come, your children who will rise up after you, and the foreigner who will come from a far land, will say, when they see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses with which Yahweh has made it sick;

and that all of its land is sulfur, salt, and burning, that it is not sown, doesn’t produce, nor does any grass grow in it, like the overthrow of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which Yahweh overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath;
even all the nations will say, “Why has Yahweh done thus to this land? What does the heat of this great anger mean?”
Then men will say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of Yahweh, the God of their fathers, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt,
and went and served other gods, and worshiped them, gods that they didn’t know, and that he had not given to them.
Therefore Yahweh’s anger burned against this land, to bring on it all the curses that are written in this book.
Yahweh rooted them out of their land in anger, in wrath, and in great indignation, and thrust them into another land, as it is today.”
The secret things belong to Yahweh our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law.

footnotes.content: Moses pauses at the threshold—Moab, not Canaan—to seal the covenant. He knows the old generation is nearly gone, and these words must land in the hearts of the young ones who will inherit. There's a tenderness in beginning here: not with thunder, but with remembrance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Your eyes have seen"—Moses names the first truth: you were there. Not hearsay, not faith in someone else's story, but your own witness of Yahweh's acts in Egypt. He begins with what they know, what they've lived, because faith builds on seen mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The trials, signs, wonders—all of it was meant to teach them. Moses isn't recounting history for entertainment; he's saying: you already know what Yahweh is like. You've seen His hand open and close, destroy and save. Look at your own past, and you'll know what to trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Yahweh has not given you a heart to know"—yet. This isn't blame; it's an invitation. Moses is saying: what you lack is not evidence but openness, not proof but willingness to listen. The Lord is about to give it, if you'll let Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty years in the wilderness, and nothing wore out. Not metaphor—literal faithfulness in the details. Yahweh sustained them so thoroughly that their clothes didn't fray. If He cares for sandals, imagine what He cares for in your soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No bread, no wine—they depended on manna and water from the rock. Yahweh taught them hunger so they'd know Him as Provider, not their own stores. Sometimes the Lord strips away what we think we need so we'll cling to what we actually can't live without: Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sihon and Og appear here as proof of victory already won. Two kings came out to fight; Yahweh struck them down. Moses is reminding Israel: the land you're about to possess is Yahweh's gift, already defended by His arm.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land given as inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half-Manasseh—already distributed. Moses shows them: what Yahweh promises, He delivers. Your brothers east of the Jordan hold deeds to land once ruled by enemies. Claim your share with the same confidence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Keep the words of this covenant and do them"—not because the Lord needs you to perform, but because obedience and flourishing are joined. You will prosper not in spite of covenant-keeping, but through it. Faithfulness is the path to a full life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All of you—heads, tribes, elders, officers, every man of Israel. The covenant isn't sealed by representatives; every person stands before Yahweh. You cannot hide behind the leader; you cannot say "the priest will covenant for me." You stand alone and together, both.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Children, wives, foreigners—even those who draw water. No one is left outside the circle. Yahweh's covenant embraces the small, the guest, the servant. If the foreigner can stand before Yahweh and be bound to His law, how carefully we should think about who we consider truly part of God's people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "That you may enter into the covenant and into His oath." Entry means passage—a crossing-over moment where you move from outside to inside, from neutral to committed. The Lord holds out the threshold; you choose whether to step through.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will establish you as His people—this is promise, not condition. If you enter, He will fulfill what He swore to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob. The covenant is Yahweh's initiative from start to finish. Your "yes" opens what His faithfulness makes real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Not with you only"—this word ripples forward. When Moses speaks here, he's making room for generations not yet born. He acts as though they are present, signing their names in this covenant too. What fidelity we show our children when we keep faith for their sake.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those not here with you today—a remarkable claim. The covenant binds not only the living but the not-yet-born, even those you'll never meet. Yahweh's word spans time. Our choices today echo forward, binding and blessing descendants we won't know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "How we lived in the land of Egypt"—Egypt as archetype of spiritual slavery. You came through the nations and saw their ways. Moses names Egypt here as the place you must learn from—the place you were and never go back to, the captivity from which only Yahweh frees you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abominations, idols—wood, stone, silver, gold. You saw what other nations trust. You watched them pour wealth into carved things. Now you know: that path leads nowhere. The second commandment says this plainly because Israel had seen it with their own eyes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "A root that produces bitter poison"—one heart turned away poisons the whole community. Not because God is tyrannical, but because covenant is communal. One person serving other gods tempts others, breaks trust, and invites judgment on all. Individual unfaithfulness becomes collective danger.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I shall have peace, though I walk in stubbornness"—the lie of the heart that refuses to obey. There is a species of pride that says: I will not listen, yet I will prosper. Yahweh says: no. Covenant-breaking and peace cannot dwell in the same house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Yahweh will blot out his name from under the sky." Nothing is worse than obliteration—to be erased as though you never were. This is not revenge but the final consequence of turning away: you cease to be part of Yahweh's story. Covenant-breaking ends in severance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Set apart for evil—the one who turned away becomes a sign to the tribes. Not a hidden judgment, but a public one. Their downfall warns others: covenant is not casual. Yahweh's faithfulness to His word means His warnings are sure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Generations to come, children who will rise, foreigners from distant lands—they will see the plagues and sicknesses. Moses sketches a future audience. Not just Israel in his time, but centuries ahead, people will read this judgment and ask why. Your choices today are read by the unborn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sulfur, salt, burning—the land becomes waste like Sodom and Gomorrah. Moses names the ancient cities as witnesses. Unfaithfulness doesn't just break a contract; it unsettles the very ground. Covenant-breaking carries cosmic weight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the nations will ask the question: Why has Yahweh done thus? The destroyed land becomes a question mark to the world. Israel's judgment is not hidden; it's a sign to all peoples of what breaking covenant costs. Your faithfulness or unfaithfulness speaks to the watching nations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Because they abandoned the covenant." Men will answer their own question: here is why the land is waste. They will name the cause—not bad luck, not Yahweh's cruelty, but their forefathers' choice to walk away. Consequences teach; judgment speaks truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They served gods they didn't know, gods Yahweh never gave them. Idolatry is not just rebellion; it's absurdity—trading the known God for strangers. And nothing Yahweh hadn't already given them. When you chase other gods, you chase shadows and lose the Light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's anger burned—not pettily, but justly. The curses written in the law book are not whims but predictable consequences. If you break trust, what did you think would follow? Faithfulness and blessing go together; unfaithfulness and curse go together. It's the order of creation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Rooted them out of their land in anger, wrath, and great indignation." Even the emotion Yahweh feels is fierce—He does not excuse covenant-breaking with silence. His fire burns for those who have betrayed His love. That intensity shows how much He cares.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The secret things belong to Yahweh; the revealed things belong to us and our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law." Readers today hear an echo in these words: God has told us enough to obey, enough to love, enough to be His. We don't need to know the mysteries of His counsel—we need to know what He asks of us, and trust the rest to His hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
